system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
user_prompt:

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale: The two symptoms with hard numbers are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), which are upstream of everything else; recovering them compounds into qualified revenue rather than buying volume. memory_73 is the one inherited record that carries its own effect sizes and an explicit failure (retention -12%, renewal failed), so promotional_pricing is disqualified without spending budget on it even under competitive price pressure — matching the competitor's entry price would trade sustainable revenue for signup count. referral_incentive (memory_57) targets established customers and does nothing for the activation/onboarding decay; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is plausible but addresses a segment showing no measured regression. That leaves simplify_onboarding vs activation_messaging, both supported only by vague consolidated summaries. I spend both verification pulls on the onboarding claims because they are the load-bearing ones for my intended action and because memory_31 and memory_86 may be two consolidations of the same underlying signup-field experiment — if so, my evidence base is half as thick as it appears. I want the original records to recover effect size, segment, measurement window, and whether the lift was measured on activation or on downstream retained revenue. Key downstream risk: cutting required signup fields (memory_31) removes the qualification data used for lead routing, and memory_44 says enterprise pipeline quality depends on the sales-assisted/demo-request path. A field-stripping change could raise activation while quietly degrading qualified pipeline — the same shape of failure as memory_73, where a top-line lift masked a retention loss. So I scope the test to SMB self-serve only, leave the enterprise demo-request path untouched, and instrument qualified-pipeline and 30-day retention as guardrails alongside completion rate, rather than reading activation alone. Standard experiment with a holdout: a smaller test cannot resolve a 4-6% movement, but I will not broadly roll out on inherited summaries whose provenance I have not yet confirmed. If verification shows the two memories are one experiment, or that the lift was never measured past week one, I downgrade to a guarded test and treat activation_messaging (memory_91) as the fallback, since in-product messaging does not touch the qualification data path.
